samples.question: This picture shows grey strands on a white page. Two ports are marked, one by a blue ring and one by an orange ring, and each ring sits on a strand. Small black squares mark the ends of strands. Grey strand is the only kind of connection: two things are joined only when you can travel from one to the other along grey strand without ever leaving it. The strands attached to the blue ring and the strands attached to the orange ring form two separate systems that never touch and never cross, so every black square is joined to exactly one of the two rings. Being close together on the page does not mean being joined. Which ring is joined to more black squares by its strands, the blue ring or the orange ring? Answer blue or orange.
